analysis.title: Americas Brokers & Crypto: Selective optimism exiting 3Q26: Retail trading inflecting positively, vs. challenging crypto backdrop - prefer brokers
key_insights: Brokers and crypto stocks under coverage are down 23% on average since 10/15/26, underperforming the S&P 500 by 16pp. Digital-asset-skewed names fell 36% and traditional retail brokers fell 19%.

Retail equity volumes turned positive MoM in October (+4%) and November MTD (+14%), the first positive MoM growth since June. Volumes are still down YoY (45% in Oct, 22% in Nov TD) and below historical seasonality, which GS reads as room for further growth.
Further retail upside is flagged from year-end seasonality, margin balance and account growth, and large-cap IPO activity (November US IPO volumes up 540% YoY MTD).

Crypto volumes are up 7% QoQ in 4Q26 TD but fell 13% MoM in October and are flat in November MTD. Crypto market cap is down 24-27% QTD to its lowest level since 2024, and GS sees a 59% R-squared between market cap and volumes, which points to further volume declines.
Crypto volumes and market cap have stayed near trough for 13 months versus a 4-month median in prior cycles, and sit 52%/65% below 4Q25 peaks.
Stablecoin market cap is down 5-6% YoY and has a ~50% R-squared to crypto market cap. GS cuts stablecoin market cap estimates by 1%/8%/9% for 2026E/27E/28E and USDC estimates accordingly.
GS trims crypto trading revenue estimates by 1%/2%/2% for 2026E/27E/28E and projects average crypto trading revenue growth of -44%/+34%/+26%.

Sports-focused prediction markets (DKeX, Underdog, Novig) gained 4pp/2pp/1pp share since August, while Kalshi and Polymarket lost 2pp/3pp. HOOD's Rothera held ~1% share, and GS expects limited impact due to the less sticky, rewards-driven user base of the new entrants.
Preferred names are Buy-rated IBKR, FIGR and HOOD on structural growth, limited direct crypto exposure and cyclical tailwinds.
IBKR thesis: 27% 2026E-28E account CAGR versus 8% for peers, 16% revenue CAGR, marketing spend up 29% from 4Q25 to 3Q26, ~85% of new accounts ex-US, and 77%/78% 2026E/27E pre-tax margins.

FIGR thesis: consumer loan marketplace volume growing 100%+ YoY, Kiavi acquisition accretive 21%/22% to 2027E/28E revenue, and a valuation of ~11.4x adj Q5-Q8 P/E, the lowest since IPO. GS is 4% above consensus on 2027E/28E revenue.

HOOD thesis: 24% 2026E-28E revenue CAGR versus a 14% peer average, ARPU rising 44% to $571, prediction markets at 12% of 2026E revenue, and a valuation of ~18.5x Q5-Q8 P/E at about the 10th percentile over 5 years.
Group valuation is ~16.5x/8.5x Q5-Q8 adj P/E and EV/EBITDA, the 2nd/4th percentile over 5 years. Traditional brokers sit at the 19th/6th percentile and crypto-centric firms at about the 1st/3rd.
Median 2026E/27E/28E EPS falls 1%/2%/1%, median 12-month price target falls 12%, and median total upside is 44%.
COIN target is cut to $181 from $210, with 4Q26E EPS moving to -$1.34 from $0.22. CRCL, GLXY, BTGO, ETOR and GEMI targets are also cut, and WLTH is unchanged.

Target cut from $210 on a weaker crypto trading backdrop, lower multiple and lower estimates. Upside is 66% from $108.78.

Target cut from $6.50 on a lower EV/EBITDA multiple and lower estimates.
Target cut from $20.50 on lower SOTP multiples for the digital assets and data center segments.
Target cut from $81 on lower USDC market cap and EPS estimates, partly offset by a 1.0x higher multiple.
Target cut from $25 on a 0.5x lower multiple and weaker crypto backdrop.
Target unchanged. The multiple rises 1.0x on a higher-for-longer rates outlook, offset by lower EPS estimates.
Target cut from $3.75. Estimates are negative and the crypto backdrop is weak, though GS still shows 108% upside to target.

sector_views.rationale: Retail trading volumes are inflecting positively with favorable seasonality, margin and account growth, and possible IPO upside. Valuations are near 5-year troughs.
Crypto market cap is at its lowest since 2024, volumes are likely to fall further, and stablecoin market cap growth has turned negative YoY.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 brokers and crypto earnings came in 3% above consensus, with diverging trends across firms (Exhibit 1 title).
HOOD GSe 4Q26E EPS $0.61 and 2026E/27E/28E EPS $3.69/$2.36 and $3.21/$3.82 per the new-estimate table (GS estimates, not reported).
COIN GSe 4Q26E EPS -$1.34 versus prior $0.22, and 2026E EPS $6.13 versus prior $6.99 (GS estimates).
IBKR GSe 4Q26E EPS $0.71 and 2026E EPS $3.58 (GS estimates).
FIGR GSe adj. EPS $1.53/$1.96/$2.36 for 2026E/27E/28E versus consensus $1.52/$1.91/$2.31 (GS and consensus estimates, adjusted).
FIGR GSe 2027E/28E revenue is 4% above consensus and adj. EBITDA (ex-SBC) is 1%/3% above consensus. 4Q26 marketplace volume is tracking above 100% YoY growth.
crypto_views: Total crypto market cap is down 24-27% in 4Q26 TD to the lowest level since 2024 and 52% below the 4Q25 peak. Industry crypto volumes are 65% below the 4Q25 peak.
Crypto trading volumes rose 7% QoQ in 4Q26 TD after a late-3Q26 acceleration driven by positive regulatory developments, but fell 13% MoM in October and were flat in November MTD.
Total crypto market cap has a 59% R-squared with trading volumes since 1Q23 and a ~50% R-squared with stablecoin market cap.
Stablecoin market cap is down 5-6% YoY after growth turned negative in October 2026. Adoption is diversifying into payments and agentic commerce.
The current crypto drawdown matches or exceeds the average of 6 prior sell-offs since 2017 (market cap -51% and volume -66% on average) and is longer than the 4-month median volume trough.
GS reduces 2026E/27E/28E USDC average market cap estimates by 1%/8%/9%.

trade_ideas.description: Long Buy-rated IBKR, HOOD and FIGR as preferred brokers and fintech exposure into improving retail trading
trade_ideas.rationale: Structural platform growth, less direct crypto exposure and cyclical tailwinds from retail trading seasonality and IPOs.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower retail engagement, faster rate cuts, and crypto market cap trending down.

risk_factors: Further crypto market cap declines could cut crypto trading volumes and stablecoin balances.
Retail engagement could fade, or PFOF regulation could hit HOOD.
Lower interest rates would hit NII at HOOD and IBKR and HELOC demand at FIGR.
Prediction markets competition from price-aggressive new entrants.
Crypto deregulatory reform may prove insufficient.
Credit and funding risk at FIGR from economic deterioration.

tension_points.bull_case: Retail equity volumes inflected up in October and November, with seasonality, margin and account growth and IPO activity supporting more growth, and valuations at 2nd/4th percentile.
tension_points.bear_case: Volumes remain down YoY (-45%/-22% in Oct/Nov TD) and below seasonality, and crypto market cap at the lowest since 2024 may weigh on volumes and broader retail sentiment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Retail volumes failing to follow historical year-end seasonality, or a reversal of the MoM growth in retail equity ADV.

theme_stances.key_argument: Retail trading volumes have inflected positively with favorable seasonality, while crypto market cap and volumes are falling.
theme_stances.evidence: we see selective upside to brokers stocks from here

theme_stances.key_argument: Lower crypto market cap could presage further trading volume and stablecoin market cap declines.
